newsitem.title: HONG KONG: INTERVIEW: Polar Air expands Asia cargo operations.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW: Polar Air expands Asia cargo operations.

text.p: Polar Air Cargo will start a new Boeing 747 freighter services from Osaka and Seoul to the United States on Tuesday (April 15), its Asia vice-president Peter Hansen told Reuters.
Bangkok was added to the privately-owned U.S. carrier's rapidly-growing route system on March 21 and Polar said it also expects to begin at least a twice weekly service to Manila in June or July.
The new Osaka service will be operated three-times-weekly to Polar's Anchorage hub, where cargo is sorted for onward flights to the U.S. or Europe via another new service to Manchester and Amsterdam.
Also from tomorrow, Polar said it will start a twice-weekly outbound freighter service from Seoul to Anchorage. Until now, Polar has only served the South Korean capital as an inbound market.

"It is an important week for us and means we have increased our capacity in Asia by 25-30 percent and now cover most of the Asian cities of consequence. Once we have added Manila later this year we will have a global system in place," Hansen said in an interview.
The only sector missing from a round-the-world service is between Delhi and Hong Kong or Osaka, which has been studied but not pursued because of inadequate demand, he noted.

"We now have a 'starburst' from Anchorage, where all our aircraft connect and then go on to Europe, to both the U.S. east coast and west coast and on to South America. It is a perfect hub-and-spoke system," Hansen added.
The Bangkok stop has been added to Polar's U.S.-Australia service. After flying from Australia, the Bangkok freighter continues onto Hong Kong, Khabarovsk and Anchorage.
Hansen said he expected the ex-Bangkok Saturday flight to attract good business.
Polar has been granted rights for two flights weekly but is starting with one initially.
"We have decided not start a second flight because once you increase the capacity there is pressure on rates," Hansen said.
"We have been pleasantly surprised by the rate situation, which is higher out of Bangkok than it is out of Hong Kong," he added.
Polar is competing with Thai Airways International, which was operating a twice weekly leased freighter service to Los Angeles but has now reduced its schedule to once weekly.
Other competition comes from a range of Asian carriers offering indirect services through their cargo hubs -- for example, China Airlines via Taipei.

"Things are going well from Bangkok after a slow start and we're moving along nicely with our local ground sales agent, Deks, which is selecting suitable business from around 40 to 50 freight forwarders," Hansen said.
Hansen said he is travelling to Manila this week to look for a local cargo sales agent and expected to add the Philippines to Polar's network by mid-summer.
